subject: Im3D node and p2define forms
evidence: The node bodies take and pass on packets with the header's RxPacketFetch inline function and RxClusterLockRead and RxPacketDispatch macros. The names are global functions in the PS2 January 2001 prototype symbol table (references/Scooby-Doo Night of 100 Frights/PROTO-PS2-2001-01-31/symbols/symtab.tsv, lines 2119, 2133 and 2134); the June 2001 table and the GC build have no such functions, and every node body here carries their code inline, so the header defines them inline (the bodies are this project's). They check the pending embedded packet, read a cluster through the packet's input slot table and call _rxEmbeddedPacketBetweenNodes and the next node's body, destroying the packet when it is still in use (bl _rxPacketDestroy at 0x80183834 and 0x80183AE4). PL2ImmStashNodeBody writes the fetch as an if/else, which gives the target's registers; the inline gives the Submit nodes theirs. _ImmRenderSetupNode's switch lists the primitive types in the order TRISTRIP, TRILIST, POINTLIST, LINELIST, POLYLINE, TRIFAN, which gives the target's compare tree (TRILIST divides by 3 with mulhwu at 0x8018306C), and keeps the caller's vertex alpha flag when it copies the default render state over a supplied one (li r27,0x1 at 0x801830FC). RxPipelineFindNodeByName stores the count of nodes left, not the index, in *nodeIndex (stw r30 at 0x80188C98, where r30 counts down at 0x80188CA8), and -1 when nothing is found (li r0,-0x1 at 0x80188CBC); the source keeps that. RxLockedPipeAddPath validates the input node through a static inline PipelineNodeIndex helper, inlined into its only caller (declared inline, since a plain static function is also emitted as a 0x4C-byte local copy the target does not have): it divides by the 0x28-byte node size (lis r6,0x6666 and mulhw at 0x80188FC4 and 0x80188FD0), checks the node is in the array (mulli and cmplw at 0x80188FE0 and 0x80188FF4) and returns -1 otherwise (li r6,-0x1 at 0x80189000); the helper's early return gives the target's branch to the join (b at 0x80188FFC), which an if statement in the caller does not.

subject: Cull and transform node forms
evidence: The cull functions test the sign of the area through RwSplitBits (the stfs and lwz pairs at 0x80181768, 0x80181A4C, 0x80181B98 and 0x80181C54), so the triangle count stays in a register across the test; the source triangle is indexed as NumElements * 3 - 3. ParallelCullProcessPacket compiles to 98.5 percent: the target computes that index as N + (2N - 3) and assigns the loop registers in another order. PerspectiveCullProcessPacket compiles to 94.6 percent: its screen-space and camera-space tests schedule the vertex loads and products differently. The partly clipped test uses RwV3dSubMacro, RwV3dCrossProductMacro and RwV3dDotProductMacro, and _CullTriangleNode picks its function before fetching the packet (li r6 before the fetch at 0x80181E50). The transform functions set the flags after the packet fetch, test 0x100 then 0x8 for the color source and 0x4 for texture coordinates (the flag values as the target has them), copy the color byte by byte, and store the clip flags as z | y | x; both compile to 98.3 percent, the gap being the registers of the packet, the strides and the or/and accumulators and the order of the x and y loads. TransformNode calls the parallel function unless the camera is a perspective camera.

subject: RwClipVertexFunc
evidence: The typedef name and parameter names are this project's own; neither prototype table names the type of PerspClipFuncs and ParaClipFuncs. The parameters are from the call in _rwForOneEdge, which passes the new camera-space vertex, the edge's two camera-space vertices, the new screen vertex and the edge's two screen vertices in r3 to r8 before its bctrl. subject: Clip node forms
evidence: The clip functions keep a result flag that only a failed resize clears (srwi. at 0x8017EF3C) and jump from there straight to the end-of-line test that destroys the packet (0x8017F450), and jump from each clipping step that leaves fewer vertices than a line or triangle needs to the drop test (blt at 0x8017EFD4), so the source uses goto for both; the clip planes go z, y, x, each pair guarded by its two flag bits, with the clip flags recomputed from the ring after the z and y steps. The resize size is the allocation plus (lines left + 12) (subf, addi, add at 0x8017EF20 to 0x8017EF2C); every resize, including the triangle's interpolant size (addi, add at 0x801801A4 and 0x801801A8), is written numAlloced + (numLines - i) + 12 (or + 24 for the triangle indices), the form under which this compiler keeps the target's operand order, and the interpolants call Init first when the allocation is 0 (bne at 0x801801AC; the explicit == 0 test gives that branch sense). The ring is set up as start, the first indices, then end (stw of end after the index stores at 0x8017EF98 and 0x80180210). The projection switches on the vertex flags masked with 0x3, 0xF and 0x3F, the masks the target compares (clrlwi at 0x8017F198, 0x8017F20C and 0x8017F18C); x and y are declared before recipZ, the FPR order the target uses. The flat-shading turn compares the ring's first index with the line's first vertex both as the loop test and after it (cmplw at 0x8017F304; the second compare is folded into the same cr0), so the color copy after the loop is unreachable in the target as here. The line stores take the second ring slot from a local computed from the same load of start (addi at 0x8017F3CC before the first sth), not from a reload. The triangle fan starts next at the third ring slot and copies it into prev before stepping it (mr r0, r7 at 0x801806AC), writes each new triangle through one pointer loaded once after the cursor moves (lwz r9 at 0x80180704), and the cull path computes the count of new vertices before the address of the last triangle (subf at 0x80180758). The triangle version caches the interpolants' stride while it moves their cursor back (lhz at 0x801807D4, before the unrolled loop at 0x801807F4). The node bodies and getters compile to the target bytes. The clip functions compile to 98.45 and 98.40 percent (lines) and 99.85 and 99.83 percent (triangles), with forms tried in tools/trial.py and tools/declorder.py and the saved-register order read from mwcc-debugger: the remaining difference is the saved-register assignment (lines: i, the result flag, the doubled stride and keep; triangles: i, the new-triangle count and the first new vertex rotate) and, in the lines, where i = 0 and the line count load are scheduled in the set-up.

subject: bavector.c square root tables
evidence: _rwVectorOpen inlines two table builders, one for square roots and one for reciprocal square roots (SqrtTableCreate and InvSqrtTableCreate in the PS2 June 2001 prototype symbol table). Each allocates 0x4000 bytes, walks 2048 mantissa steps from 1.0 (addis 0x1000 per step) through the double sqrt inline with frsqrte (0x80165E88), stores each result less 0x1FC00000 or 0x20000000 through a stack word and then the second half of the table, and returns 0 after an out-of-memory error. src/rwsdk/src/plcore/bavector.c builds the table with RwSplitBits locals for the step, the root and the stored value, and writes each value through a U32 pointer into the table. It reaches 97%: the target places the reciprocal builder's stack words below the square root builder's in a split this source does not reproduce, and in each of the four table loops this build loads the step's word (lwz r4) before the table store, where the target loads it after the pointer step (for example 0x80165F38), so the unit stays NonMatching.

subject: babinary.c byte swap as an expression

evidence: The imported MSL units (src/MSL_C.PPCEABI.bare.H/, msl profile in configure.py) compile to the target under GC/1.3 and link byte-identical. Twelve of them differ under GC/1.3.2: alloc.c (4 of 10 functions match), mem_funcs.c (0 of 4), mbstring.c (2 of 5), qsort.c (0 of 1), strtold.c (__strtold differs), strtoul.c (__strtoull differs), ansi_fp.c (7 of 11), char_io.c (3 of 4), file_io.c (1 of 5), e_exp.c, e_pow.c and s_atan.c (0 of 1 each); the others compile identically under both, and no MSL unit matches only under GC/1.3.2. -char signed: is_utf8_complete (0x800EAB94) sign-extends the first byte with extsb. at 0x800EABA8 before its zero test, and without -char signed GC/1.3 emits cmplwi there; without -char signed (with -char unsigned), six units differ: ansi_fp.c matches 8 of 11 functions, printf.c 6 of 13, scanf.c 0 of 4, mbstring.c 3 of 5, qsort.c 0 of 1 and strtold.c 1 of 2 (__strtold differs); every other MSL unit, the math units included, compiles identically either way. -inline auto,deferred: MWCC emits deferred functions in reverse source order, and the target's function order is the reverse of the source order of the Metrowerks-ordered upstream files (for example ac-decomp 09ca8e8 mem.c and mem_funcs.c, and tww 02de6b7 mbstring.c); without it each object's .text comes out reversed. This replaces the earlier per-object reading, which rested on libmap probing MSL with the runtime profile only, whose flags lack -char signed and deferred inlining: mbstring.c, printf.c, scanf.c and string.c then placed only under GC/1.3.2. With the msl profile, printf.c, scanf.c and string.c also place under GC/1.3 (config/GIHE78-rev0/lib_units.tsv), and the imported mbstring.c and string.c match under GC/1.3. -fp_contract on: the fdlibm kernels use fused multiply-add (the target's __kernel_cos at 0x800F1B6C has 9 fmadd/fmsub-class instructions and __ieee754_acos 40). With -fp_contract off, ten fdlibm units differ (e_acos, e_asin, e_exp, e_pow, e_rem_pio2, k_cos, k_rem_pio2, k_sin, k_tan, s_atan), the same as the upstream tww 02de6b7 and tw2004 11985bc files compiled verbatim with their own headers; every other MSL unit, the other 18 math units included, compiles identically with it on or off, so the setting is library-wide rather than per object.

subject: TRK_flush_cache start parameter
evidence: TRK_flush_cache's first parameter is declared u32 in src/TRK_MINNOW_DOLPHIN/trk.h and flush_cache.c, where ac-decomp 09ca8e8 declares void*. Its callers pass addresses: TRKTargetAccessMemory, TRKTargetSupportRequest, TRKTargetFlushCache, __TRK_copy_vectors, and TRKTargetAccessExtended2 (0x800E3C18) through the inlined TRKPPCAccessSpecialReg. Both declarations compile every caller to these bytes, so the target does not decide between them. With void*, TRKTargetAccessExtended2 matches only through ac-decomp's double conversion (void*)(u32)access_func: written as access_func or (void*)access_func it compiles 8 bytes shorter (0x430 against 0x438). With u32, each caller converts once, (u32)access_func, (u32)addr, (u32)dest and (u32)start, and the u32 values start and gTRKCPUState.Default.GPR[6] pass with no cast. This project uses u32 because that form needs no conversion that exists only for code generation. The asm body uses the register only as an address, so the target fixes neither the parameter's type nor its name.

subject: TRKTargetAddStopInfo u16 truncation
evidence: TRKTargetAddStopInfo sends the registers truncated to 16 bits. In the loop over the 32 GPRs it loads each one and passes it to TRKAppendBuffer1_ui32 through clrlwi r4,r0,16 (0x800E3874), and in the loop over the FPRs it passes the low word of each to TRKAppendBuffer1_ui64 through clrlwi r6,r0,16 (0x800E389C). src/TRK_MINNOW_DOLPHIN/targimpl.c writes these as (u16) casts, as ac-decomp 09ca8e8 does; the instructions change the values sent, so the casts are behaviour the target shows, not a form chosen to match. The clrlwi at 0x800E384C comes from TRKAppendBuffer1_ui16's u16 parameter, with no cast in the source.

subject: TRK_MINNOW_DOLPHIN/targsupp.s
evidence: src/TRK_MINNOW_DOLPHIN/targsupp.s assembles to .text of exactly 0x20 bytes matching this range: four 8-byte functions, each twui r0,0 then blr. They sat inside the targimpl.c range before. Animal Crossing's splits, generated from the disc's static.map, list targsupp.s as an object of its own with comment:0; dtk's map import sets comment:0 only for an object the map names with a .s suffix, and an assembled object has no compiler .comment section (ac-decomp 09ca8e8 config/GAFE01_00/splits.txt, 0x800A8130-0x800A8150, align:16); The Wind Waker's splits, generated from maps/framework.map, list TRK_MINNOW_DOLPHIN/ppc/Export/targsupp.s the same way (tww 02de6b7 config/GZLE01/splits.txt, 0x80337020-0x80337040, align:16). The source uses .balign 16 to match. This split leaves out comment:0: without a .comment section dtk records no original addresses in the split object, objdiff then reports the unit's section with no virtual_address, and tools/public_report.py cannot place it on the map. The .comment section is not linked into main.dol. Linked as Matching; the complete DOL relinks byte-identical (SHA-1 c77fb29d39b5898933e8ef4d1ccd2ddac404554e). Both .text edges are exact because the assembled object fills the range.

subject: __shr2i
evidence: Compiler helper for long long a >> n, called from compiled code in the target (for example dolphin/pad/Pad.c). Probe: a C function performing long long a >> n, compiled with GC/1.3 and GC/1.3.2 (-nodefaults -proc gekko -align powerpc -enum int -fp hardware -O4,p), emits a bl to __shr2i instead of code, so the C operator itself cannot be its source. The target computes n - 32 once, with addic. r9,r5,-32 at 0x800E5DA8, and performs the sraw at 0x800E5DB8 before the ble at 0x800E5DBC that tests it. Under GC/1.3 and GC/1.3.2, a C rendering whose shift is unconditional (t = hi >> (n - 32); if (n - 32 > 0) lo |= t, or the same with int m = n - 32) compiles to addi with a separate compare (addic. or cmpwi), and a conditional shift (if ((m = n - 32) > 0) lo |= hi >> m) reaches a single addic. but places the sraw after the ble. Later compilers (GC/3.0a3, GC/3.0a5.2, Wii/1.0) do emit the target's opcode sequence for int m = n - 32; t = hi >> m; if (m > 0) lo |= t, so the instruction sequence alone is not decisive. What holds is the register use: the target keeps its temporaries in r8, r9 and r10 while r0, r6 and r7 stay unused, and none of the probed compilers leaves r0 unused for this code. The same r8/r9/r10 template appears in __shl2i and __shr2u, which have instruction-level markers of their own. This is the weakest of the runtime.c assembly rows: it rests on register allocation and on its family's template, not on an instruction C cannot express. Linked from the asm function in src/Runtime.PPCEABI.H/runtime.c.

subject: ngcsnd.c memset

subject: binkread.c string.h
evidence: src/bink/src/sdk/decode/binkread.c does not include string.h and declares memmove itself. The target calls memset and memcpy the way GCC 2.95's builtins expand them. Every memcpy call is set up with crclr 4*cr1+eq, constant or variable size: checksound (0x80113BDC, 0x80113C2C, 0x80113C70), BinkOpen's track_index copy (0x80114FC8), BinkDoFrame (0x80115B1C, 0x80115B50, 0x80115B70) and BinkGetTrackData (0x801177EC). memset gets crclr only with a constant size: BinkOpen (0x80114138), BinkClose (0x80116458), BinkGetSummary (0x801167C4) and BinkOpenTrack (0x80117658); the variable-size memsets in dosilence (0x80113A38, 0x80113A48, 0x80113A5C) and BinkDoFrame's mask clear (0x80115BF4) have none. The `b` structure assignment in BinkOpen copies inline and makes no call. Prototypes compatible with the builtins (void* memset(void*, int, U32) and void* memcpy(void*, const void*, U32)) give identical bytes, as does no prototype. string.h's prototypes take size_t and conflict with the builtins; with string.h included, ProDG 3.5 changes six more functions (checksound, BinkOpen, BinkDoFrame, BinkClose, BinkGetSummary, BinkGetTrackData). memmove, which GCC 2.95 has no builtin for, is called without crclr (BinkDoFrame, 0x80115838).

subject: intelendian lwbrx
evidence: intelendian byte-swaps each word of the buffer in place with lwbrx r0,r9,r3 (0x80117A04; r9 is set to 0 before the loop at 0x80117A00) and stw. ProDG 3.5 and 3.9.3 have no C form for lwbrx: neither the shift-and-mask swap nor assembling the word from its four bytes produces it, and GCC 2.95 has no __builtin_bswap32. src/bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcfile.c writes it as one __asm__ statement with the index in an "b" operand of 0, which ProDG loads into r9 outside the loop as the target does. Approved by the project owner (Lucas, 2026-10-28) as a documented exception.

subject: ngcfile.c memmove prototype
evidence: src/bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcfile.c declares memmove itself and does not include string.h. The crclr 4*cr1+eq before the memcpy calls (0x80117AE8, 0x801181C4, 0x80118220) and the memset call (0x801183C0) comes from GCC 2.95's builtin memcpy and memset, which ProDG expands into library calls; the memmove call at 0x80117CB8 has no builtin and no crclr. subject: ngcfile.c volatile fields
evidence: The BinkIO counters in include/bink/binkio.h and the filepos, bufempty and cancelling fields of src/bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcfile.c's private NGCFILE area are volatile. The target reloads them after storing them and keeps their accesses in source order: BinkFileReadHeader stores filepos and reloads it (stw r0,136(r31) then lwz r11,136(r31) at 0x80117B6C/0x80117B70); CancelReadRequests stores cancelling before the cancel and after the polling loop (0x80117F88, 0x80117FAC), which the callback reads (0x80117C5C). Under ProDG 3.5, dropping volatile from error, reading, bytes_read, total_time, fg_time, buf_size, buf_peak, cur_size, cur_used, filepos, bufempty or cancelling changes at least one function; busy is decided by Bink's frame code rather than this file: BinkNextFrame stores 1 and then 0 to it with no access between (stw 0x80115DE4 and 0x80115DF0), and a non-volatile busy loses the first store. idle_time and bg_time are declared volatile like the other counters; dropping it changes no byte of this unit, and the target does not decide them yet. The other NGCFILE fields are not volatile: the target keeps their values in registers across stores.

subject: BinkAudioDecompressOpen frsqrte
evidence: The target takes the square root of half (the ip allocation size) with an inline reciprocal square root estimate and three Newton steps: frsqrte f0,f11 at 0x80120074, then three rounds of fmul and fsub steps against the 0.5 and 3.0 double constants (0x801A8770, 0x801A8778), and multiplies the estimate by the input. subject: read_rle_samples single-bit reads

subject: read_rle_samples variable-width read

subject: YUVSTATE
evidence: The YUV blit state S at 0x801DAF20, as the ngcrgb.c converters use it: two output rows, two luma rows, the U and V planes and two alpha rows at +0x0 to +0x1C, each read at the start of a converter (the output rows are advanced and stored back there; the other rows are stored back at its end), and the output pitch and buffer base at +0x44 and +0x48, which GetTiledRgbLoc reads. 0x4C bytes, bfbb's extent of S. The ngcyuy2.c row functions use +0x0 to +0x14 the same way, each read at the start of a row function and advanced at its end. yuv.cpp, which owns S, stores the colour offset indexes at +0x20 to +0x28 (YUVSTATE.g, .b, .r); +0x2C to +0x43 has no access in the target and stays padding. The row pointers are U8*: the yuv.cpp row functions step them in bytes (addi 1 after lbz), and the ngcrgb.c and ngcyuy2.c converters scale their steps to bytes. A project name, not a claim of the original name.

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcrgb.c plane pointer order
evidence: The ngcrgb.c converters take their plane pointers from S in the order u, v, y0, y1, with a0 and a1 first in the alpha converters (a0, a1, u, v, y0, y1); they read *u++, *v++, *y0++, *y1++ and then *a0++, *a1++ in the loop, and store the pointers back to S in the order u, v, y0, y1, a0, a1. ProDG schedules these accesses, so the target's instruction order is not the source order: YUV_32_4x2_even loads y1, u, v, y0 (lwz 12(r9), 16(r9), 20(r9), 8(r9) at 0x801243D8, 0x801243E0, 0x801243E8, 0x801243F0). The exact functions fix part of the order, measured by compiling the alternatives (objdiff fuzzy match): in YUV_32_4x2_even, taking y0 and y1 from S before u and v (99.69%), storing them back as y0, y1, u, v (99.54%) or u, v, y1, y0 (99.52%), or declaring v before u (99.71%) no longer matches, while reading *v++ before *u++ or declaring y1 before y0 still matches. Taking a0 and a1 last breaks YUV_32a_4x2_even (89.63%) and YUV_32am_4x2 (99.59%). Two exceptions are fixed the same way: YUV_16m_4x2 and YUV_16mx2_4x2 take y1 from S before y0 (y0 first gives 99.58% and 99.62%), and YUV_16a4m_4x2 and YUV_16a4mx2_4x2 read *a0++, *y0++, *a1++, *y1++ in the loop, the target's load order (lwz 0(r25), 0(r28), 0(r26), 0(r27) at 0x80126E60, 0x80126E64, 0x80126E70, 0x80126EAC, and 0x801270A8, 0x801270AC, 0x801270B8, 0x801270F4); reading both luma rows first gives 87.96% and 87.88% against 90.32% and 91.06%. The near misses follow the same order and are not evidence for it.

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcrgb.c r, b, g pointer order
evidence: Each pixel pair computes r = YUVTables[3][v] and b = YUVTables[0][u] before g = YUVTables[2][u] + YUVTables[1][v], and a 32-bit pixel is clamp_ytable[y][r] (clamp_ytable is a table of U32 pointers, one per luma value). YUV_32_4x2_even keeps the YUVTables rows in r15 (row 3), r16 (row 2), r17 (row 1) and r18 (row 0) (addi at 0x801243DC, 0x801243E4, 0x801243EC and 0x801243AC) and loads them in the order row 3 by v, row 1 by v, row 2 by u, row 0 by u (lwzx at 0x8012445C, 0x80124484, 0x8012448C, 0x8012449C). The target fixes only that g comes last: computing in r, g, b order leaves 20 words differing and b, g, r order 12, while b, r, g also matches. The source keeps r before b; that part is not decided by the target.

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcrgb.c grouped mono32 loads

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcrgb.c U16 luma intermediate

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcrgb.c (U16) table reads

subject: bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcrgb.c parenthesised g sum
evidence: In the 16-bit colour converters the green pointer is clamp_g + 256 + (YUVTables[2][u] + YUVTables[1][v]): the target adds the two table entries together (YUV_16_4x2_even add r6,r6,r10 at 0x80124E70) and adds the clamp_g base to the scaled sum after it (add r6,r6,r18 at 0x80124E94, r18 = clamp_g+0x400 from addi at 0x80124DDC). subject: YUY2_4x2Helper and YUY2_x2_4x2Helper pair count
evidence: The colour helpers process two luma words per pass and count passes with an arithmetic shift of the word count (srawi r3,r29,1 at 0x80127BFC and 0x80127D2C), so the count is S32, and the pass counter is unsigned: src/bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcyuy2.c writes U32 i = n >> 1 and while (i--). An odd last word is finished with the chroma halfwords (lhz at 0x80127CC8/0x80127CD0 and 0x80127E58/0x80127E5C), which the source reads into U16 locals beside a new local for the luma word; with U32 chroma locals 6 words differ, and with the loop's yy for the luma word 16 differ.

subject: pixel-doubling helpers luma masks
evidence: YUY2_mx2_4x2Helper and YUY2_x2_4x2Helper isolate the four luma bytes of a word into four registers before combining them (clrrwi, rlwinm 0,8,15, rlwinm 0,16,23 and clrlwi at 0x80127F54-0x80127F80), so src/bink/src/sdk/decode/ngc/ngcyuy2.c writes each output word with the masked byte repeated, for example (yy & 0xFF000000) + ((yy & 0xFF000000) >> 16), which GCC computes once. subject: LenBPLossless cntlzw
evidence: LenBPLossless takes the bit length of each coefficient magnitude as 32 minus its leading zeros (cntlzw r9,r9 at 0x8012D5B4, after the clrlwi r9,r9,16 of the absolute value). GCC 2.95 has no leading-zero builtin (__builtin_clz came with GCC 3.4) and emits cntlzw only for comparisons with zero, so src/bink/src/sdk/bitplane.c writes the count as an __asm__ statement in its CNTLZW macro, the same macro as expand.c and binkngc.c. Under ProDG 3.5 and 3.9.3 __builtin_clz is an external call and __builtin_ffs computes find-first-set (neg; and; cntlzw). The project owner approved inline asm for the three bitplane.c encoder uses (2026-10-28), with one row per use.

subject: LenBPLossless and encoders quad entry compare
evidence: When a quad is split, LenBPLossless, WriteBPLossless and WriteBPLossy test the length byte of the new entry against the current bit plane and only build the full entry for the store: in LenBPLossless the clrlwi r0,r11,24 and cmpw at 0x8012D8B8 compare the byte, and slwi/addi 0x300/or at 0x8012D8C4-0x8012D8CC form the entry stored with sthu. src/bink/src/sdk/bitplane.c writes the test as (U8)(*lp + ((x << 10) + 0x300)) != n and repeats the expression in the store (LENQUAD, WRITEQUAD, LOSSYWRITEQUAD). Computing the entry once into a U16 local changes the register allocation of the whole pass (98 lines of LenBPLossless differ).

subject: VARBITSPUT bit count copy
evidence: WriteBPLossless writes each coefficient magnitude with n - 1 bits (VarBitsLens is indexed by the count, for example lwz VarBitsLens+0x10 at 0x8012DD68), and the target keeps that count in a register of its own for the mask, the length update and the carry shift. src/bink/src/sdk/bitplane.c copies the count into a local (U32 _n = (n)) at the top of the VARBITSPUT macro. Using the macro argument directly changes the register allocation of WriteBPLossless (231 lines differ); WriteBPLossy compiles the same either way.

subject: WriteBPLossy refinement loop
evidence: WriteBPLossy's loop over the significant coefficients increments the index right after loading sig[i] (lbzx r0,r7,r11 at 0x8012F73C, addi r11,r11,1 at 0x8012F740), before the bit test. src/bink/src/sdk/bitplane.c writes it as i = 0; while (i < nsig) VARBITSPUT1(vb, sig[i++] & bit);.
